extracted.intended_audience: eRA Commons users and institutional administrators (SOs, AAs, PIs, reviewers, account managers)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and security standards for registering institutions and users, creating and managing eRA Commons accounts, password policies, federated login linking, roles and privileges, and use of the demo/training site.

rubrics_metrics.name: Password Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for creating eRA Commons passwords: must be at least eight (8) characters long (no blank spaces), case sensitive, and must contain a combination of at least three (3) of the following character types: uppercase letters, lowercase letters, numeric characters, special characters (! # $ % - _ = + < > *).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The following special characters are NOT allowed: @, &, or a period (.). Password may NOT contain your Username, may NOT start or end with a number, cannot be reused within one year, and must be changed every 90 days. Passwords created/changed by IC Account Administrators must be changed at first login.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporary Password Validity
rubrics_metrics.description: Temporary passwords sent to users via email are valid for only 48 hours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Temporary passwords must be changed to a permanent password of the user's choosing within that 48-hour window; temporary passwords are used to gain initial access for password change.

rubrics_metrics.name: First-Time Login Password Change
rubrics_metrics.description: First-time users logging in with a temporary password will be prompted to change the temporary password to a permanent password.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Steps: enter temporary password as Current Password, enter new password and confirm, then Submit. The Change Password screen displays password creation standards and will show a confirmation if the new password meets NIH standards; otherwise an error message displays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expired Password Reset
rubrics_metrics.description: If your current eRA Commons password has expired, you cannot link accounts and must change the expired password before linking or further access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To reset an expired password: enter Current Password, enter New Password and Confirm, then Submit. The new password must conform to the standards shown on the Change Password screen and becomes effective immediately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account Lockout Policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Accounts are locked after six (6) consecutive unsuccessful login attempts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users can click the Forgot Password/Unlock Account? link to unlock their account; Commons will generate and send a temporary password to the account owner's email which is active for only 48 hours. For locked accounts, SOs can also unlock and reset accounts using the Manage Accounts feature in the Admin module.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resetting a Locked Account (SO process)
rubrics_metrics.description: When an account is locked due to invalid login attempts, the institution's Signing Official (SO) must unlock the account and reset the password using Manage Accounts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accounts Management module has online help for unlocking and resetting passwords. If the account is not locked but password forgotten, users may use Reset Password themselves via the Forgot Password link.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reset Password Process (self-service)
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure to reset a forgotten password: select Forgot Password/Unlock Account? link, enter User ID and Email address, Submit; Commons generates a new temporary password and sends it to the email in the user profile.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After receiving the temporary password, log into Commons and create/enter a new permanent password as prompted. All passwords validated against the Password Policy requirements. You must be able to access the email used to create your Commons account to receive the temporary password.

rubrics_metrics.name: Password Security Best Practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Security guidance about entering and storing passwords.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Your old password may re-appear if browser cache/history not cleared; do not use the browser save-password option; always re-enter your password whenever logging in to Commons to maintain account integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federated Institutions/Organizations Sign In (pilot)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pilot functionality that allows users at participating registered organizations to use their organization credentials to log into eRA Commons and optionally link those credentials to an existing Commons account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Steps: select organization from dropdown on Commons welcome page, Sign In, enter organization credentials on organization's managed sign-in page. If Commons determines organization credentials are associated with your Commons ID you will be logged in; if not linked you'll be prompted to link via Link Institution/Organization Credentials with eRA User ID screen. Validations occur with your organization — failures must be addressed with your organization. eRA cannot help with organization-managed screens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions Preventing Account Linking (common causes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Situations that will prevent linking of organization credentials to your Commons account: using a system-assigned temporary password, having an expired Commons password, or having a locked Commons account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If using a temporary password you must first change it to one of your choosing. If your password is expired, log in with the expired password to be presented the Change Password screen. If account locked, use Forgot Password/Unlock Account? link or contact SO. In other cases contact the eRA Service Desk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role-based Access Model
rubrics_metrics.description: User roles determine which Commons features are accessible and what tasks users may perform; roles are assigned (largely by the SO) and the modules visible depend on assigned roles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Roles range from trainee to scientific to administrative roles; the IAR role is enabled by an SRO. Modules appear on the navigation bar if you have access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account Administrator (AA) privileges
rubrics_metrics.description: AA facilitates administration of Commons accounts (typically located in Central Research Administration).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AA can create accounts and modify all Commons roles except IAR and FCOI roles, and can create affiliation between existing PI or IAR Commons accounts and the institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative Official (AO) privileges and constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: AO is an institutional official (may be same person as SO in some workflows) with privileges for account creation and viewing grant info but not authorized to submit reports or view summary statements/priority scores.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AO can create all accounts other than IAR, TRAINEE, and FCOI; update Commons accounts they created; view status and award information for institution grants; create affiliation between existing PD/PI or IAR accounts and the institution. AO cannot view summary statements/priority scores and cannot modify the Institution Profile. AO and SO authorities should not be combined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assistant (ASST) privileges
rubrics_metrics.description: ASST may be delegated to perform tasks on behalf of a PD/PI depending on granted authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ASST may edit their own PPF data, edit PD/PI PPF if delegated, edit PD/PI progress report data if delegated, view PD/PI Grant Status if delegated, and perform PD/PI xTrain functions (except submit to agency) if delegated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Business Official (BO) privileges
rubrics_metrics.description: BO manages trainee grants and uses the xTrain module; has signature/administrative authority for training grants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BO can view trainee roster, list of grants, grant summary, routing history, PDF-formatted appointments/amendments/terminations; initiate, update, route, and submit Termination Notices (TN) if authorized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial Conflict of Interest (FCOI) role and privileges
rubrics_metrics.description: FCOI role is assigned by the SO to manage the Financial Conflict of Interest reporting process at the institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FCOI can initiate, view/edit, delete, and submit FCOI reports. FCOI responsibilities can be shared via FCOI_ASST or FCOI_View roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: FCOI Assistant (FCOI_ASST) privileges
rubrics_metrics.description: FCOI_ASST assists in working on FCOI reporting and can perform data entry and edits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Privileges include initiating FCOI, searching FCOI, viewing, editing, and deleting FCOI reports. Assign FCOI_ASST to users who need authority to do more than view.

rubrics_metrics.name: FCOI Read-Only (FCOI_View) privileges
rubrics_metrics.description: FCOI_View provides read-only access to search and view FCOI information entered by the institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assigned by SO to users who only need to search and view FCOI data. FCOI_ASST should be assigned to those who need to edit or initiate entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal Financial Report (FSR) role
rubrics_metrics.description: FSR role is assigned for completing Federal Financial Report responsibilities for grants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FSR users have privileges to submit FFRs on behalf of the institution. An account with only the FSR role can only perform FSR tasks. FSR duties may be combined with SO or BO/AO depending on institutional workflow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internet Assisted Review (IAR) role
rubrics_metrics.description: IAR users (selected by SROs) can critique and score submitted grant applications using the IAR module.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IAR privileges include editing personal PPF and Reviewer address data and using IAR to submit critiques and preliminary scores for meeting-enabled applications. IAR role is often auto-added for PD/PIs enabled for a meeting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program Director/Principal Investigator (PI) privileges and constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: PI (PD/PI) directs NIH-supported research projects; the PI role allows management and viewing of grant-specific information but has some delegation limits and combination constraints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PI can edit personal PPF, delegate edit authority of their PPF, view status of grant applications where designated PI, view assembled images of submitted applications, view Study Section/Meeting Roster, view review outcomes and summary statements, view Notices of Award, delegate authorities (with limits), use xTrain functions for training grant items (roster, grants list, grant summary, routing history, PDFs), initiate and manage appointments/re-appointments/amendments in xTrain, initiate progress reports (and delegate), and submit a progress report when given SO authority. PI users cannot delegate authority to submit appointments to the Agency. PI role should not be combined with SO role but can be combined with IAR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signing Official (SO) privileges, constraints, and responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: SO has institutional authority to legally bind the institution in grant-administration matters and has broad account and institutional profile privileges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SO can register applicant institution in Commons, create/update Institution Profile (IPF), create/delete/update all Commons accounts except IAR and TRAINEE, create affiliations between PD/PI and institution, submit grant applications via Grants.gov as AOR if registered, view status of all institution-originated applications and related errors/warnings, view assembled images, reject grant applications to address warnings, view award information for all institution grants, submit JIT info for a PD/PI, delegate and submit progress reports, submit Final Progress Reports, submit one-time No-Cost Extensions on behalf of PD/PI, and assign the FCOI role. An SO cannot view summary statements or priority scores. SO role should never be combined with a PI role.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sponsor (SPONSOR) privileges
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponsor supervises research training experiences for fellows in xTrain and is associated with fellowships at the institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sponsor can view trainee roster and list of grants, review and route Termination Notices to BO, initiate Termination Notices for fellows who left the institution, and delegate Sponsor authority to others. SO or AO can add Sponsor role to an account.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trainee (TRAINEE) privileges
rubrics_metrics.description: TRAINEE role manages electronic appointments for awarded training grants in the xTrain module.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TRAINEE can view PDF-formatted appointments/amendments/terminations, update and route their own appointments/amendments/terminations, and view routing history.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registering Institutions: required information and process
rubrics_metrics.description: One-time institution registration is required to access eRA Commons; registration creates SO (mandatory) and optional AA accounts and activates institutional presence in Commons after NIH review and approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You must have a valid/verifiable DUNS number before registering. Only authorized organization officials may be SOs (examples: President/CEO, Executive Director, University President/Dean/Chancellor). Steps: select Register Grantee Organization, Read instructions, Register Now, complete required fields. All fields with red asterisk (*) are required; at least one address line (Street 1) is required. Institution Name max 100 chars, Official's Title max 240 chars. User Name min 6 and max 20 characters (numbers and letters allowed, no spaces), account names must be unique. After submission NIH sends address confirmation email to SO; NIH reviews the registration and sends approval/rejection; if approved SO confirms and signs to activate organization in Commons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demo (Commons Demonstration Site) creation and usage rules
rubrics_metrics.description: A fully functioning demonstration site mirrors the Commons production environment with sample data to practice creating sample institutions, accounts, and manipulating grant applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To create a new demo account: select Demo Facility link, fill in required fields (asterisked), create at least an SO and a PI account (required) and unique usernames (min 6, max 20 characters); submit and save. A confirmation lists username and password — copy the information. Demo accounts allow practicing functions such as submitting RPPRs or FFRs and working with xTrain sample data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admin Module: Accounts Management capabilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The Admin module contains features for Account Management and Delegations; access and available features depend on assigned user role.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From Admin > Accounts you can Manage Accounts, perform Advanced Search, and Change Password. Administrators (e.g., SO) can perform advanced searches to locate PIs eligible for continuous submission and can search for accounts within or outside the institution as allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Displayed password standards and validation
rubrics_metrics.description: Change Password screen lists the password creation standards that must be followed; passwords are validated against the Password Policy requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the new password meets standards a confirmation displays; if not, an error message displays. Users should clear browser cache/history if old password autofills or confuses entry.
